title: ReconDreamer: Crafting World Models for Driving Scene Reconstruction via Online Restoration

output_modality.value: Dynamic driving scene reconstruction (Gaussian-splatting based) rendering novel-trajectory video; a world-model restorer outputs cleaned video.

control_signal.value: Novel ego trajectory for rendering (lane shift 3 m, 6 m, lane change); restorer is conditioned on degraded rendered video, 3D boxes and HDMaps.

control_mechanism.value: DriveRestorer, fine-tuned from a world model, takes masked degraded video as control condition; progressive data update feeds restored novel-trajectory frames back into reconstruction training.

base_model.value: DriveDreamer-2 world model (built on Stable Video Diffusion) fine-tuned as restorer; Street Gaussians as main reconstruction backbone, also PVG, S3Gaussian, Deformable-GS.

datasets.value: Eight highly interactive Waymo scenes, split into 40-frame segments, front-facing camera only.

metrics.value: NTA-IoU, NTL-IoU, FID on novel trajectories, plus a user study win rate.

controllability_evidence.value: At 6 m lane shift versus Street Gaussians: NTA-IoU +24.87%, NTL-IoU +6.72%, FID +29.97% relative; versus DriveDreamer4D with PVG NTA-IoU +195.87%, user-study win rate 96.88%.

closed_loop.value: No. Novel-trajectory rendering evaluated offline; closed-loop simulation is only the motivation.

notes: Primarily a reconstruction method using a world model as restorer, not a driving world model with a user control input; control family set to other. Stride ablation notes larger strides exceed restorer capacity (page 8-9).
